options: A model where only one developer is allowed to commit at a time
Every developer maintains their own permanent, never-merged branch
Everyone works off a single shared branch, merging small changes into it frequently
A strategy specific to database code with no application-code equivalent
questions.explain: Trunk-based development favors small, frequent merges into one shared branch rather than long-lived separate branches.

questions.q: What extra wrinkle does database code have that application code mostly doesn't, per this lesson?
options: Database code can't be stored in Git at all
A schema is stateful — a branch can't simply be discarded once its migration has run against real data
Database branches automatically merge without any review
SQL doesn't support comments, making code review harder
questions.explain: Once a migration runs against a real environment, real data depends on its effects — unlike app code, which just gets replaced when a branch merges or is dropped.

questions.q: Why should feature branches for database work stay short, according to this lesson?
options: The longer a branch lives, the further its version of the schema drifts from what's running in test or production, making reconciliation harder
Short branches are required for a database project to build at all
Long branches make Schema Compare stop functioning
Git technically forbids branches older than 48 hours
questions.explain: Extended drift between a long-lived branch and the live schema compounds the reconciliation problem the longer it's allowed to continue.

questions.q: If a feature branch's migration adds a column to a test database and the branch is later abandoned, what actually has to happen?
options: The entire test database must be deleted and rebuilt from scratch every time
Nothing — the column automatically disappears when the branch is deleted
Someone has to explicitly handle removing or reconciling that column, since the data doesn't disappear just because the branch did
Git automatically reverses any migration tied to a deleted branch
questions.explain: A deployed migration's effects on real data persist independently of the branch's existence in Git — someone must deliberately address it.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the real constraint for database code, regardless of branching model chosen?
options: Choosing exclusively between trunk-based development or feature branches, with no other factor mattering
Whether the team uses SSMS or Azure Data Studio
Migration sequencing — ensuring schema changes apply in a consistent, predictable order across every environment
The number of developers on the team
questions.explain: Whichever branching model is used, predictable migration sequencing is what actually keeps environments consistent.
